Who this class is for

For anyone who puts everyone else first

  • People who look after everyone around them, and would like a kinder way to include themselves on the list.
  • Anyone who hears “that’s a bit selfish” in their head the moment they think about their own needs.
  • People who have read about self-care and want a clear, practical way to make it part of an ordinary week.
  • Anyone who would like to say what they need, at work and at home, calmly and with confidence.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover together, live

Why “selfish” got a bad name

The difference between selfish and self-caring, and why meeting your own needs is part of caring well for others.

Taking back your power, step by step

An introduction to the 7 steps from my book How to Be Selfish, and where to start this week.

Advocating for yourself

Simple ways to name what you need and ask for it, so you feel safe and confident doing it.

Rest that restores

My 8 Pillars of Rest, and how to find small pauses in a full day instead of waiting for a holiday.

The Vitality Wheel

A walkthrough of my Vitality Wheel, and how to use it as a quick, kind check-in with yourself.

Meet Suzy

Hi, I’m Suzy Reading

I’m a Chartered Psychologist, yoga teacher and health and fitness coach, and I’ve spent 30 years in health and wellbeing.

I’ve written 11 books, including How to Be Selfish (Penguin, 2025) and The Self-Care Revolution, and I’ve been the named Psychology Expert for Neom Organics, Kalms, Treatwell and Tempur. 87.4k people follow along on Instagram.

Before you save your seat

Who is this class for?

Adults who would like practical, psychology-informed ideas for looking after themselves while looking after others.

What if I can’t make it live?

Register anyway. Everyone who signs up gets the replay.

Because the first step should be easy. Come, take what helps, and decide afterwards if you want more support.

I hear this more than anything else: “It all sounds lovely, Suzy, but I don’t have time for me.”

That’s what working together one to one is for: a plan that fits your real week, and someone in your corner while you practise it.

Ad creatives · Video scripts · Meta

Video ad scripts

Three talking-to-camera scripts, each around 30 to 45 seconds, in your own voice. Each ends with an on-screen “Educational content, not medical advice.”

Script 1 · “Selfish isn’t a dirty word”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“As a psychologist, I think we’ve got the word ‘selfish’ completely wrong.”

Body

“There’s the kind of selfish that takes from others. And there’s the healthy kind: noticing what you need and making room for it. That second kind doesn’t take anything away from the people you love. It’s what lets you keep showing up for them.”

CTA

“I’m running a free live masterclass on how to be selfish, the healthy way. Tap Sign up to save your seat. The replay is included.”

Shot: talking to camera, soft blush backdrop, on-screen text “Selfish, the healthy kind”.

Script 2 · “Rest isn’t a reward”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Rest isn’t something you earn once everything else is done.”

Body

“So many of us treat rest as the prize at the end of a to-do list that never ends. In my work I talk about eight different pillars of rest, and most of them take minutes, not a weekend away.”

CTA

“I’ll walk through them in my free class, the You Matter Too Masterclass. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: walking outdoors in the woods, cut to a simple “8 Pillars of Rest” graphic with botanical line art.

Script 3 · “Speak up for yourself”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Three small ways to speak up for what you need, from a Chartered Psychologist.”

Body

“One: notice the need before you talk yourself out of it. Two: name it simply, without a long apology. Three: ask, and let the answer be whatever it is. It gets easier every time you practise.”

CTA

“Join my free live class. Sixty minutes, replay included. Tap Sign up to save your seat.”

Shot: talking to camera, counting on fingers, numbers 1 to 3 on screen in plum.
